- Unintentional weight loss of 4.6 kg over 6 months — systemic manifestation consistent with malignancy  
- No hemoptysis, fever, night sweats, or chest pain — makes active infection or advanced local invasion less likely, but not incompatible with early-stage NSCLC  
- Normal chest X-ray — does not exclude lung cancer; many early NSCLCs are radiographically occult on CXR  
- Normal CBC (WBC, Hgb, platelets) — consistent with early-stage NSCLC (not yet causing paraneoplastic cytopenias or leukemoid reaction)  

[GAPS]  
- Absence of chest CT findings — critical for confirming presence, location, size, and characteristics of a pulmonary nodule/mass  
- No PFTs — needed to assess baseline obstructive vs. restrictive pattern and surgical operability  
- No sputum cytology or bronchoscopy results — definitive tissue diagnosis pending  
- No PET-CT or staging data — limits assessment of metastatic spread (e.g., adrenal, bone, nodal)  
- No biomarker testing (e.g., EGFR, ALK, PD-L1) — required for treatment planning but not for initial diagnosis  

[DIAGNOSIS]  
Non-small cell lung cancer
